A1: Building identity, classification, purpose group, storeys and spaces.
A2: All linked storeys, including records with no optional classification.
A3: Spaces, their storeys, uses and areas within each building.
A4: Distinct spaces by use, with missing uses retained as unbound values.
A5: Membership counts across 16 reporting classes. Classes may overlap.
A6: Contained or adjacent fabric elements and located fire-protection equipment.
B1: Compliant, noncompliant and undetermined outcomes for the 44 selected checks.
B2: Actual and required fire resistance for each selected element, including missing values.
B3: Compartment-wall classification inferred from an assigned fire-separating role.
B4: Trace each REI finding through its requirement, clause and regulatory source.
C1: Risk units, installation and explicit space membership.
C2: Distinct boundary records grouped by unit and condition state.
C3: Conditions, evidence availability and adequacy for each boundary aspect.
C4: Unit-level P = U + C + G, counting each boundary once despite multiple evidence links.
C5: Missing or conflicting states and contradictions between evidence status and links.
C6: Trace a risk finding through its fire scenario, boundary and evidence.
D1: Event, task and assessment relationships, with planned and actual times kept separate.
D2: Assessments and compliance findings linked to the requirements they check.
D3: Inspection date, workbook revision, worksheet and source-record identifiers.
E1: Service deadlines, physical condition, functional tests and criterion-level outcomes.
E2: Source records and evidence supporting equipment and door inspection findings.
E3: Separate totals for devices, selected checks, deficient checks and affected devices.
